questions.question: What is the purpose of a Look-Up Table (LUT) in a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)?
options: To store large blocks of volatile memory for data caching.
To implement any arbitrary Boolean function by configuring its internal truth table.
To manage external input/output operations and device communication.
To provide a dedicated Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) for integer computations.
To route clock signals uniformly across the entire chip.

questions.question: In a typical CPU pipeline, what is the primary role of the 'Decode' stage?
options: To execute arithmetic and logical operations on operands.
To fetch the next instruction from the Instruction Cache or main memory.
To write the results of an operation back to a register or memory location.
To determine the instruction type, identify operands, and retrieve their values (if from registers).
To access data from the Data Cache or main memory based on memory addresses.

questions.question: In Design For Testability (DFT), what is the main benefit of incorporating 'scan chains' into a digital IC?
options: To reduce the dynamic power consumption during normal operation.
To improve the chip's immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI).
To facilitate deterministic testing of sequential logic elements (flip-flops and latches).
To increase the overall processing speed of the integrated circuit.
To enable on-chip voltage regulation for various power domains.

questions.question: Which dynamic branch prediction scheme employs a global or local history register (BHR) to index into a Pattern History Table (PHT), where each entry typically contains a saturating counter (e.g., 2-bit) to predict the branch's outcome based on past patterns?
options: Static Branch Prediction (Always Taken/Not Taken)
Bimodal Predictor
Gshare Predictor
Tournament Predictor
Profile-Guided Prediction

questions.question: In the context of formal verification for digital ICs, what is the primary advantage of Model Checking over Formal Equivalence Checking (FEC)?
options: Model Checking can automatically generate comprehensive test vectors for gate-level simulation.
Model Checking is primarily used for comparing two different implementations of the same design (e.g., RTL vs. gate-level).
Model Checking can mathematically prove or disprove specific temporal properties (e.g., safety, liveness) about a single design.
Model Checking operates at significantly faster speeds, enabling real-time verification of complex System-on-Chips (SoCs).
Model Checking eliminates the need for any simulation-based verification entirely.
